_about: Hand-read labels for E072. Every entry names a (account, brand) family that a person reading the raw descriptor strings would call a RECURRING PAYMENT: a subscription, a plan, or a monthly bill. Read from `python3 relabel.py` output; no detector output was consulted. Frozen before eval_arms.py ran. Accounts are the CORPUS.json ids; brands are the `probe_undergroup.brand()` token.
_labelling_rule: A family is POSITIVE if the reader, seeing the raw strings and the dates and amounts, would say 'this is one thing I pay for on a schedule'. It is EXCLUDED (not counted as negative) when the family mixes a recurring charge with unrelated purchases under one brand token -- AMAZON is the standing example, where a cardholder's grocery orders and their Prime membership share the token. Excluded families are listed in `excluded_families` with the reason, so the exclusion is auditable and not silent.
_counts_note: G4 requires >= 12 hand-verified subscription merchants. The gate is on DISTINCT MERCHANTS, so (a03 SPOTIFY) and (a04 SPOTIFY) count once.

_lost_to_corpus_exclusions.reason: a04 is a budget app's export that concatenates an Actual block and an original Chase block, both with a column named `Payee`. It is excluded as ambiguous, so the corpus loses its LONGEST-VERIFIED subscription: 49 Spotify rows over 1461 days, a monthly charge confirmed across four years. That is a real loss of the strongest positive evidence in the corpus and it is stated rather than absorbed. a04 also produced the best-looking under-grouping numbers in the first probe run, while the loader was reading the app's already-cleaned payee column, so its absence removes a defect as well as data.
a26's 'Description' column holds hand-written budget categories and its amount column runs to 7392, i.e. spending totals rather than transactions. Excluded as not a bank export.

_excluded_families_note: `excluded_families` is the audit trail for every candidate family that was read and NOT labelled a recurring payment. A family is excluded rather than counted as a negative when one brand token mixes a subscription with unrelated purchases (AMAZON is the standing case), or when the reader could not resolve what it is. Precision is therefore measured against a corpus that omits ambiguous families, which is stated as a limitation on every precision figure.
